title: Spectral-front identities for periodic Navier-Stokes and a conditional obstruction to uniform pointwise Osgood closure
description:
This is not a solution to the Clay Navier-Stokes problem, in either direction.

For strong solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus, the spectral bandwidth obeys an exact modal identity yielding the monotone quantity Lambda = log N_0^2 - (1/2 nu) int K D, hence a bandwidth-dissipation dichotomy: finiteness of the action int K D forces the solution to be global, so any finite-time breakdown makes the action diverge. The action admits the exact representation int K D = int |du/dt|^2/D + nu^2 int H_2/H_1 + nu log(D/D_0), and is dominated pointwise by both the Serrin (infinity,2) and the critical L^3 gradient actions.

Conditionally on one open lattice-sum hypothesis, certified in exact rational arithmetic at small band sizes, an explicit coherent critical-spectrum family forces every uniform pointwise majorant Phi in K <= Phi(log N_0^2) to be of exponential class, so no Osgood-admissible majorant exists and the dichotomy cannot be closed by that route.

The repository additionally records the candidate blow-up mechanisms that were tested and rejected, each with exact-arithmetic or interval certificates, and separates proven, conditional, and rejected material explicitly.
notes: Machine-assisted research repository. Internal review passes were performed by AI agents; they are not human peer review.
